item.title: Understanding Rotary Positional Enbeddings (RoPE)
item.description: Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) is an advanced technique for encoding positional information within transformer-based language models. Unlike traditional positional embeddings that add or concatenate position vectors, RoPE introduces position by rotating the query and key vectors in multi-dimensional space. This geometric approach enables transformers to capture both absolute and relative positions more effectively, especially for long sequences. In this article, we’ll cover the motivation behind RoPE, its mathematical foundation, key advantages, and practical implementation.
